inspectionMethod: All packet render and preview paths were inspected directly or through hash-verified review sheets. Four native frames were also inspected directly at 768x1408. Eight connected/independent native assemblies were inspected at logical cell128 through reviews/round04-native-assemblies.png; original source images and fixed target were inspected again. All38 retained browser screenshots were inspected at original screenshot scale in19 labeled connected/independent sheets. Packet phone and four-view previews, backgrounds, fixed regression and whole-image worst were directly inspected. The image source/hash mapping is retained in reviews/round04-independent-image-audit.json.
observations: Compared with the original cyan blank slab, all four candidate facings visibly describe substantial irregular stone masses with broad worn facets and recessed crevices. Rectangular attached plates have been replaced by coherent native relief. N/S side faces and E/W crown/end views all carry readable stone structure.

The cyan upper planes, cobalt middle and darker blue lower volume preserve identity. The base retains visible facets and crevices at128 and32 cell pitches instead of becoming the original near-black empty block. Broad matte highlights are soft, without a white gloss ribbon, neon edge or horizontal lighting preference.

Three-module connected and independently captured native assemblies read as the same continuous formation. In the actual updated browser consumer, the independent N/E/S/W runs remain visually continuous at128 and32 pitch and the retained47.3 fractional case. Fractional root/pan phases and light/gray/dark/transparent contexts expose no new endcap, crown step, alpha gap, vertical border, shading reset or color seam.

The saved old round03 consumer comparison shows the prior fractional source-over join line. Round04 uses the actual shared SpriteScene world-raster composition before the final browser scale/pan; its current source bytes match the packet-bound dependency snapshots. Approval applies to that updated consumer, not the historical independent nested-SVG sampling path.

The reported whole-image residuals are real but not a material visible seam defect. Independent remeasurement of all19 retained screenshot pairs matches their whole-image metrics. The worst N128 phase(.25,.5) has7 pixels over5 levels, maximum19, at periodic stone-crease pixels away from native cut columns160.25/288.25. The true cut band in that case has maximum2 and no pixels over5. W47.3 has2 isolated pixels with maximum14 in the broad projected profile region; the outer-silhouette alpha maximum10 in E128 is likewise localized. I inspected these regions enlarged and at actual size; they do not form a continuous connector line or meaningful coverage gap.

No material dead spot, clipping, directional cast shadow, target-image card, floating decal, coplanar shimmer or distracting halo was found in the required static views or repeated consumer previews. Tiny geometric pinches visible in enlarged native crease intersections do not disrupt intended-size stone readability.
remainingDifferences: The target has rounder, more individually swollen stones, more varied small pebbles and sharper painterly highlight accents. The native result uses broader and quieter carved facets with fewer small decorations; it remains a clear material improvement toward the agreed soft cartoon stone style.

The locked full-cell connector profile retains a geometric crown-to-side plane transition and straight external cut planes. Those are intentionally more modular than the rounded ImageGen outline. The lower surface remains darker, but its stone information is visible.
Identical modules repeat the same stone motif, which is visible as a pattern. The module boundaries themselves do not create an extra border or lighting discontinuity.

Connected versus independently rendered geometry is not byte-identical. Small retained antialiasing and crease-sampling residuals are documented above and accepted on actual visual evidence, without relaxing the requirement for seamless visible joins.
